svg.title: TOPAK B10 — Rules of engagement live in three places, and the floor gains a federation stage of fourteen forbids, none written
svg.desc: ADR-0067 puts a mission's rules of engagement in three places: standing rules in the one Cedar floor, the same at every plane and every governor; a mission's mechanical rules in a promoted bundle compiled to Wasm, which can only refuse; and judgments about the world nowhere in the admit path (ADR-0007). The floor gains a stage, federation, after workflow: fourteen forbids, FD1 to FD14, each from the record it enforces, and two existing entries relaxed. ADR-0067 is Proposed, an overlay and not the archetype. No entry is written as Cedar, gated or built, and since no floor is ratified, nothing here can be in force (§5).
svg.text: TOPAK · B10

text.tspan: Rules of engagement live in three places, and the floor gains a
stage of fourteen forbids, none written

svg.text: ADR-0067 puts a mission's rules of engagement in three places: standing rules in the one Cedar floor, the same at every plane and every governor; a mission's mechanical rules in a promoted bundle compiled to Wasm, which can only refuse; and judgments about the world nowhere in the admit path (ADR-0007). The floor gains a stage, federation, after workflow: fourteen forbids, FD1 to FD14, each from the record it enforces, and two existing
entries relaxed. ADR-0067 is Proposed, an overlay and not the archetype. No entry is written as Cedar, gated or built, and since no floor is ratified, nothing here can be in force (§5).

text.tspan: None: nothing here can be in force (§5)

svg.text: Proposed means nothing here is in force. The custodian put two things: rules of engagement as a promoted Wasm bundle ⟨5⟩, and the Cedar floor in force with them ⟨7⟩; and answered that one floor serves the whole tree ⟨Q8⟩ and that this is an overlay ⟨Q11⟩. Every other choice is the drafter's, and the entry ids are placeholders. C1 applies: the entries are forbids on privileged paths, and two existing entries are relaxed, each of which routes as a relaxation (ToO §3.2). C2, C3 and C4 do not
apply on the drafter's reading while this is an overlay. R1 (2026.11.10) changed one entry, FD10, to follow ADR-0063 R1. One author, one day, and no policy text.

text.tspan: Rules that need a judgment about the world

svg.text: ADR-0007: no semantic judgment is an enabling condition
"Syntactic lift (mechanical, total extraction from a constrained call interface) is permitted in any zone. Semantic lift is prohibited in the admit path. Classifier output enters as an Observer
finding, and findings may only subtract authority, never add it."
"A classifier is usable as a trigger for deny, quarantine, or eviction."
Extension (09.12): totality, non-vacuity and discrimination gates run on the floor itself, not only on operational bundles. §7 asks them of this stage.
ADR-0067 states the rule as "no semantic judgment is an enabling condition", and its provenance note says ADR-0007 was taken as ToO and the proposal give it, not re-read.

text.tspan: Why the floor does not carry a mission's rules (Options)

svg.text: The floor would change with every mission, and it is the one artifact that is verified.
Rules enforced by the stack are not rules. The stack is Byzantine.
ADR-0030 §1's engine table, whole: where the bundle tier runs a sidecar and a local engine
returns true from the lease's revision
returns anything else from the lease's revision
Refuse. Authoritative: no fallback
is unreachable, errors, times out, or serves another revision
The local engine decides iff it holds the lease's revision
— and the local engine holds no such revision
Refuse: the bundle "cannot be reached"
At an autonomous plane and on a governor, §2 leaves only the local engine. On this diagram's reading, the last two rows are then the whole tier: the local engine decides iff it holds the lease's
revision, and otherwise the bundle refuses. Every admit records which engine decided (ADR-0030 §1).

text.tspan: A mission's rules are a promoted Wasm bundle ⟨5⟩ (§2)
A bundle can express what a mechanical lift can supply

svg.text: Time windows, as ranges of the plane's ticks (ADR-0064).

text.tspan: Which entries a seat kind may use.

svg.text: Counts, within a vehicle or across vehicles.
Which entries are ordered (ADR-0062 §3): the bundle marks an entry ordered where the tally wants agreement across vehicles, and the archetype marks none
A refusal of a report to a peer topic, by seat kind, rate or label.
A refusal of an entry once the stack has read a peer's report in the clear (ADR-0065 §3).

text.tspan: Lists that come from a declared source and carry its label.
Tightening: by promotion, or faster by a narrower intent

svg.text: A commanded plane tightens by promoting a bundle, which is appended (ADR-0059 §2).
A commander tightens faster by narrowing a value in the next intent (ADR-0060 §2): an ordered admit signed by one operator, which adds nothing the tally did not
vote (ADR-0059 §3's table).
At a plane whose charter allows it, and otherwise it goes up the tree.
That asymmetry is the one the corpus already has between subtraction and grant: "adding takes a quorum, and denying is local" (ToO §7.10, as ADR-0059 §3
quotes it).

text.tspan: At an autonomous plane and on a governor, the Wasm engine is the only one

svg.text: The reference has the path: topak-bundle loads a signed bundle into an in-process engine bound to the lease's revision, as the fallback when the sidecar cannot
answer (mechanism/README.md: "local OPA WASM fallback bound to the lease's bundle").
Not taken: a sidecar on the vehicle (Options). Nothing of this record is built on a vehicle.

text.tspan: A stale bundle on a vehicle is safe in the direction that matters

svg.text: It can refuse too much, and cannot allow what the floor refuses (ToO §3.1: stale bundles are monotone-safe).
The floor is consulted first, and a floor deny is never sent to a bundle (ADR-0030 §1).

Every new entry subtracts (§3). The stage would follow workflow in floor/proposed/README.md. The amber row is the one R1 changed: FD10's governor clause follows ADR-0063 R1, which charges an ordered entry to the governor's own account as a lease is (Outstanding.tla's finding 1, M_ORDEREDFREE). No other entry changed (History).

text.tspan: How to read the last column

svg.text: A module is not the floor. Each states a property of a model of its own record, at small constants. None reads Cedar text, and
none shows that an entry, once written, says what its row says. It proves nothing about the stage.
Matched by section only: a cell is filled where the property's header names the record and section in "From". It is empty where
no module's property does.
FD2: LeaseWithinChain (Federation) is about the same check, and states ADR-0059 §4, §5, not §1, so it is not listed.
Release.tla assumes no floor: "the floor's refusals (FD5, FD6 and FD9, ADR-0067) are a second check in series that is not
assumed here", so its properties rest on the interlock alone.

Each stage is the previous one plus the entries one batch of records asks for, so a stage can be adopted without the ones after it (floor/proposed/README.md). How a stage is made and gated: build.py writes the stage's schema, floor and cases; cedar validate and cedar run-tests; then run-gates.py drives the genesis gate runner unchanged and adds routing controls for the new entries, each weakened candidate classed a relaxation and each strengthened one a tightening. For
federation none of this has run. The README also says of every stage: the floor trusts its inputs, the facts the lift supplies.

text.tspan: The lift supplies these, and the floor trusts its inputs

svg.text: As floor/proposed/README.md says of every stage: the facts are the lift's, and no policy computes them.

text.tspan: On a vehicle the lift is the governor's

svg.text: It lifts its own facts: elapsed time, position, the lease's count, an entry's extent (ADR-0062 §1). So the floor there trusts what one
component measures (Consequences).

text.tspan: "In force" is a precondition no record here can meet (§5), and four judgments no policy expresses (§6)

svg.text: The floor is ratified when a bootstrap reviewer finds it fit, and no test for fitness is written (G11 §2.2 and item 87; ADR-0029 A4, as §5 cites them).
So nothing ADR-0067 adds can be in force until a floor is ratified, whatever is written or gated of it (Consequences).

text.tspan: For this stage, whether the standing rules are the right ones is a legal judgment as much as a technical one.

svg.text: A grant seat with that named role is suggested (drafter's suggestion).
The floor enforced today, emergency, is genesis-provisional: gated, pinned and enforced, ratified by no batch (ADR-0030 A3; B8).
Identification, intent, necessity and proportion are judgments about the world (§6). Each is enforced by nothing in this set of records.
A judgment about the world. No policy here expresses it.
A judgment about the world. No policy here expresses it.

text.tspan: For an irreversible effect: the person at the

svg.text: Their judgment (ADR-0066 §5). The mechanism records who acted, on what, through which vehicle and when; not why, and it checks none of it.
It "cannot tell a person from a program holding the person's key" (ToO §3.3, as ADR-0066 §5 quotes it).

text.tspan: For everything else: at most an Observer's objection, after the fact

svg.text: A classifier's output enters the system only as a finding, and a finding may subtract authority and never add it (ADR-0007; ToO §2.2).
Negative consequence: the parts of a mission's rules that matter most are enforced by nothing here.

every stage does

forbids are in clearSet

items a peer originates, since a relayed lease does enable a permit; §7's wording is the unrevised one
The two relaxations are routed as ToO §3.2 has a relaxation routed

text.tspan: One author, one day, and no policy text.

svg.text: The entries in Cedar, the gates, and the monotonicity check (§7).
A captured vehicle discloses the rules it carries (the NATO reading, F3), and nothing says whether a bundle or an envelope carries restricted.
Sibling planes under one parent: a forbid that their envelopes are disjoint, or the overlap declared (the NATO reading, N1).
Who judges that the standing rules are the right ones (§5).

Closes: nothing. Carries a debt against: nothing while this is an overlay. Depends on ADR-0059 to ADR-0066 (what the entries forbid), ADR-0030 (bundles cannot add authority; the floor on a verified evaluator), ADR-0007 (no semantic judgment is a lift) and ADR-0058 (overlays; Proposed).
